plan: The script loads and validates the supplied measurements, then treats rows as one ordered time series rather than independent runs. It compares time-only, width-plus-time, and lag-augmented shear regressions using contiguous blocked validation. A primary 0.1-second width change and its growth direction are added to the augmented model; lag and smoothing sensitivity are reported without selecting a single best setting. It also estimates the growth-versus-decline shear contrast only over overlapping width ranges and reports coverage. Residual autocorrelation and a moving-block bootstrap summarize time-series uncertainty descriptively, not as replicate-level inference. The script saves plots and prints data checks, prediction metrics, and the conditional contrast; any apparent memory remains an association, not proof of mechanism.

analysis: The reported matched-width contrast and bootstrap are not correctly matched/valid. Growth and decline are pooled across the whole time series, so shared time trends can create the contrast; furthermore the bootstrap samples blocks from `idx` (already filtered rows) but applies those positions as original row indices, mixing unrelated observations and invalidating its interval. Also `np.nan_to_num` makes unavailable lag values zero, although the common interval excludes those rows for the primary fit but sensitivity eval may have distinct masks. Use contiguous original-index moving blocks, and estimate the contrast conditional on width (and time), restricted to genuine support overlap; interpret forecast scores cautiously since expanding TimeSeriesSplit tests later regimes only.

analysis: The analysis has a substantive modeling bug: `fit_predict` places `width` and `time` in the spline transformer but sets `n_smooth = min(2, train_x.shape[1])`; for the time-only baseline, its sole time feature is smooth as intended, but `X_aug` appends lag delta/direction/interaction as linear terms. More importantly, the reported bootstrap contrast resamples rows as blocks but preserves precomputed direction labels, not recomputing lagged deltas on each resampled trajectory; this does not estimate uncertainty for the stated matched growth/decline contrast. The 0.1 s blocks are also shorter than indicated residual dependence (ACF1=0.865), so intervals are not reliable. In addition, expanding-window `TimeSeriesSplit` tests only later periods, confounding validation with temporal regime change; the augmented model does not improve versus the baseline (slightly worse RMSE/MAE), and the contrast CI includes zero. Fix by recomputing direction from each bootstrap block/trajectory with boundary handling, selecting blocks based on residual autocorrelation, and reporting that current evidence does not support predictive memory.
